note: Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's official list as carried by the kit starter. Guides are our own words, built from the official descriptions; nothing here has been verified in the game yet, and no specific location or step is claimed without a cited source.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum: it pops automatically once the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is no separate task to do for it. Work through the roadmap in order — story first, then strangers, collectibles, activities and the combat and heist trophies — and this one closes the set. Nothing about it can be missed, because it only depends on the other 54.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing — this is the first story mission of the game, so it should pop very early in a normal playthrough. Because it is tied to one named mission, treat it as missable until replay is confirmed: do not skip the mission or rush past its objectives. If you are following the story in order, you cannot really go wrong here.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter's final mission is done. Keep the story moving in order and finish every mission the chapter gives you before wandering off to free-roam activities. As a chapter-completion trophy it is story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops at the chapter's close. Chapter 2 is a natural stopping point for a first sweep of side content, but do the story missions first so the chapter actually completes. Story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 by finishing its story missions in order. By this point in the game most of the map and side systems should be open, so it is a good moment to clear any stranger strands that have appeared — but finish the chapter itself before moving on. Story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4's missions to earn this one. Chapter 4 is the last numbered chapter, so after it pops you are into the endgame: before the final mission, sweep up any stranger strands and collectibles you have been putting off. Story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the game's final mission — the gold trophy for finishing the story. Before starting it, do a cleanup pass: stranger finals, collectibles and activities are much easier to finish before the credits roll than after, if free-roam after the ending is limited. This is the single most story-locked trophy in the set, so do not rush into the finale unprepared.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish the named story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies pop when that one mission is complete, so play it when the story offers it and do not skip its objectives. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed — if the mission can only be played once, there is no second chance in the same playthrough.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions usually have setup steps before the main job, so follow the story prompts and finish the mission itself rather than only its preparations. Story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the named story mission Child's Play when the story offers it. Like the other named-mission trophies, it pops on mission completion, so take the mission when it appears and see it through. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Play it when the story offers it and finish its objectives in full — named missions are the one-shot moments of the story, so do not leave it half-done. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown. The name points at the airport (VCIA), so expect a vehicle or aircraft set-piece, but the trophy itself only needs the mission completed. Story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name suggests a bigger set-piece mission; play it when offered and complete all of its objectives. Story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own checklist — the gold companion to the platinum. This is a long grind, not a single mission: story, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the rest of this list all feed into it. Track it in this guide's checklist and leave it for the cleanup stage of the roadmap; it pops when the game's completion counter itself hits 100%.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across free roam — jumps, near-misses, airtime and the like, as the game counts them. This is a pure volume trophy: it builds up naturally while you drive around Leonida doing everything else, so do not grind it early. If it is your last silver, pick fast cars and long open roads and keep chaining stunts between other objectives.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types at least once — racing, bowling, the arcade, fishing, the Shooting Range, drone races, stunts and the other open-world activities the game offers. This is a sampler trophy: one go at each type is enough, so work down the list early and use it as a tour of what the game offers. Not missable, since activities stay available in free roam.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the hardest pure-skill trophy on the list: work through the challenges one weapon at a time, learn each one's target pattern, and replay the ones you silver until they turn gold. The range is repeatable in free roam, so nothing here can be missed — but expect this to take real practice.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. Drone races are a learned skill — fly the course a few times to memorize the gates before going for the win, and do not be discouraged by early losses. All 14 locations stay open in free roam, so this is not missable.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — 20 distinct race events, not the same race 20 times. Work through the race list systematically and tick each one off in this guide as you win it, so you can see which events are still un-won. Races stay available in free roam, so nothing here can be missed.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a stranger encounter tied to Cal, so it comes from his strand of missions rather than from casual fishing. Play Cal's strand when it appears and take the fishing challenge when it is offered. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed: a one-off challenge against a named character may not come back.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish a full game at an arcade machine, not just start one. Pick the shortest or easiest cabinet you find and play it to its end. Arcades stay open in free roam, so this is not missable and makes a nice early trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger strand. Stranger strands are chains of missions for one character, so keep taking Andy's missions whenever they appear on the map and finish the chain. The final mission is the one-shot moment of the strand, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger strand. Work through Kenton's missions in order whenever they appear, and do not leave the chain half-finished going into the finale. The final mission is story-locked, so treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger strand. Take Billy's missions as they appear and see the chain through to its end — stranger finals are the kind of trophy that is easy to leave behind and hard to recover. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands across Leonida. There are more than 8 strangers in the game, so you have some choice — but each strand is a chain, so finish the ones you start instead of collecting half-finished chains. This silver sits on top of the five named stranger finals, so clearing those five is most of the way there. Treat strands as missable until replay is confirmed.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger strand. Play Randy's missions in order as they appear and finish the chain before the final story mission, when stranger content may close off. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger strand. Keep taking Tyrone's missions whenever they show up and see the chain through — the final mission is the payoff and the trophy. Treat it as missable until replay is confirmed.

trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a stranger task, so it comes from Bret's strand rather than from free hunting. Sets stay completable in free roam, so nothing here can be missed — but do not leave all the hunting to the very end.

The count is the whole game here: 100 spots across Leonida, so chip away at it on every trip instead of saving it for a single grind. Locations stay available in free roam, so it is not missable, just long.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's scattered mini-objectives, which add up across every system you touch. Play broadly: races, stunts, the range, collectibles and stranger work all throw challenges at you, and 50 of them is a natural total by the late game. Not missable, since challenges stay open in free roam.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose the cops and escape. The partner matters — this only counts with them along, so do it during a moment when they are with you rather than solo. Plan an escape route before you start: a fast car and open road beat hiding in an alley. Repeatable in free roam, so not missable.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level — the trick is the streak, not the robberies. Pick three shops close together, move fast between them, and keep the cops on you the whole way; if the wanted level drops, the chain breaks and you start over. Do it with your partner along, and repeatable in free roam, so not missable.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive or ride each one and it counts as discovered. This builds up fast if you keep swapping cars instead of sticking to one favourite: every new model you get into is progress. Vehicles stay discoverable in free roam, so it is not missable.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus. Set it up: find a spot with at least five enemies grouped together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them before it ends. If you only get three or four, back off and try again in a busier fight — Combat Focus is repeatable, so this is not missable.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the airport. In plain terms: get into an aircraft at the airport and take off without going through the normal channels, which is almost certain to draw the law. Bring a fast approach, expect a wanted level, and get airborne before the response closes in. Repeatable in free roam, so not missable.
sources: Our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This one is about the Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke rather than an instruction, so the honest guide is: get into a Rhino tank situation and see it through, which most likely means dealing with one in combat or taking one for a drive. The exact trigger is not pinned down by the official description, so we will not invent one — check back once players have confirmed it in-game. Not missable, since tanks appear in free roam.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — stealth is the whole point, so a loud smash-and-grab will not count. Plan the approach, avoid cameras and witnesses, and get in and out clean; if you are spotted, leave and try again. Repeatable in free roam, so not missable.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault is a full job — get in, crack the vault, and get away clean — so treat them one at a time and keep a getaway vehicle ready before you start. Five successful escapes is a silver's worth of work, but vaults stay robbable in free roam, so nothing here can be missed.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida, so find one in free roam, stop it, take its cargo and get away before the response arrives. One clean robbery is enough — but if the escape goes wrong, the trucks keep coming, so it is not missable.

This is a touring trophy: drive, fly and walk through every named area until the map is filled in, and use the count (52) to know how far along you are. It pairs naturally with the WAiNK and vehicle trophies, so do them on the same trips. Not missable in free roam.

trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — and follow through, meaning finish a game there rather than just starting one. Head to that alley, play a full game, and the trophy should pop. A simple, repeatable free-roam activity, so not missable.

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count up to 500, so this is about volume, not one big decision. Every choice the game offers, in missions and in free roam, adds to the total; just keep choosing rather than avoiding decisions, and the count climbs on its own. It is a long passive grind, but not missable.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — succeed at something on your second try after failing it once. This is one of those trophies that almost earns itself: fail an activity or mission objective, then succeed at the retry, and it should pop. Do not force it; just keep playing and retrying things, and it will come. Not missable.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the game's odd-event trophy. These moments hide in the corners of Leonida: unusual sights, encounters and secrets that are easy to walk past. Explore off the beaten path, poke around strange places, and keep your eyes open; the trophy pops when you find one. Not missable in free roam.

Line up a slow pass past a pedestrian, swing as you go by, and keep the vehicle moving. It may take a few tries to land cleanly, but it is repeatable in free roam, so not missable.
